case_analysis.critical_finding: For C(2), all bosonic oscillators are non-interacting in the undeformed algebra ([b_i, b_j] terms are only diagonal), and fermionic oscillators form the CAR. The cross brackets [b^s, a^σ] vanish identically in the undeformed algebra. Therefore, δf(b^s, a^σ) = [b^s, f(a^σ)] + [a^σ, f(b^s)] = 0 always! This means γ_gb = δf only if γ_gb = 0, i.e., all gb parameters must vanish.

case_analysis.observation: Similar analysis to n=1. The bosonic oscillators b_1^±, b_2^± interact only through [b_i^-, b_i^+] = 1 (no b_1-b_2 terms). The fermionic oscillators a_1^± satisfy {a_1-, a_1+} = 1. Cross brackets [b_j^s, a_1^σ] still vanish in undeformed algebra.
case_analysis.triviality_constraint: By same reasoning as n=1: (δf)(b_j^s, a_1^σ) = [b_j^s, f(a_1^σ)] + [a_1^σ, f(b_j^s)] Since f(a_1^σ) ∈ span{b_1±, b_2±} and f(b_j^s) ∈ span{a_1±}, the brackets [b_j^s, b_k^±] and [a_1^σ, a_1^±] vanish in the algebra. Therefore δf restricted to deformed pairs always equals 0. Triviality requires all gb parameters = 0.

case_analysis.observation: By the same structural argument: C(n+1) has only [b_i^-, b_i^+] = 1 interactions, no b_i-b_j interactions for i≠j, and [b_j^s, a_1^σ] = 0 undeformed.
case_analysis.triviality_constraint: General result extends to all n: γ_gb = δf (up to scalar) ⟺ all gb_{σ,j,s} = 0

theorem.title: Triviality Theorem for C(n+1) Inhomogeneous Deformations
theorem.statement: An inhomogeneous deformation γ_gb of C(n+1) = osp(2|2n) defined by [b_j^s, a_1^σ] = -gb_{σ,j,s} κ is trivial (i.e., γ_gb = δf for some odd linear map f) if and only if all gb parameters vanish: gb_{σ,j,s} = 0 for all σ,j,s.
proof_outline: 1. The deformation cocycle γ_gb is supported only on pairs (b_j^s, a_1^σ)
2. In the undeformed C(n+1) algebra, [b_j^s, a_1^σ] = 0
3. The coboundary δf(b_j^s, a_1^σ) = [b_j^s, f(a_1^σ)] + [a_1^σ, f(b_j^s)]
4. Since f reverses parity: f(a_1^σ) is bosonic, f(b_j^s) is fermionic
5. No bosonic-bosonic or fermionic-fermionic brackets give non-zero results
6. Therefore δf(b_j^s, a_1^σ) = 0 identically for any choice of f
7. Triviality requirement γ_gb = δf forces γ_gb = 0, hence all gb = 0
theorem.key_insight: The structural sparsity of the oscillator algebra (only diagonal bosonic interactions and no intrinsic fermionic-bosonic coupling) makes the coboundary operator unable to produce the deformation cocycle unless the cocycle itself is zero.

conclusion.reason: Coboundary cannot generate the deformation cocycle
